mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing the discount rate applied to future corporate earnings and increasing the present value of equities, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods of declining FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll growth above 200k per month signals strong labor market demand, which supports consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in < 40% of instances when PAYEMS exceeds 200.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts below 1.1 million units signals weakening consumer confidence and reduced durable goods demand, leading to lower corporate capital expenditure and weaker earnings expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST < 1100.0 (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production and a rise in the unemployment rate signals a weakening manufacturing sector and labor market stress, indicating an imminent economic slowdown that reduces corporate profitability and triggers negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO < 107.0 and UNRATE > 5.2 (t-test p > 0.05) or interaction Rank IC < -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the federal funds rate above 0.25% within a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, increasing borrowing costs and reducing corporate investment, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS > 0.25 (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < -0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above 445 billion dollars, combined with rising housing starts, indicates strong aggregate demand, boosting corporate revenues and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both RSAFS > 445000.0 and HOUST > 1150.0 (t-test p > 0.05) or interaction Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the unemployment rate below 5.0% combined with a rise in non-farm payrolls above 200k signals a labor market overheating, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting the Fed to tighten policy and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE < 5.0 and PAYEMS > 200.0 (t-test p > 0.05) or interaction Rank IC < -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth below 1.5% annualized, as measured by GDPC1, signals a weakening economy, reducing corporate earnings and investor confidence, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 < 1.5% annualized (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
